cards.text: Israel just rebelled against the house of David, and King Rehoboam, Solomon's son, escaped to Jerusalem in his chariot (2 Chronicles 10:18-19). Now he's home. I bet he's not taking this well.

cards.question: Rehoboam is back in Jerusalem after Israel rebelled. True or false: he gathers an army to fight Israel.

cards.text: He calls up 180,000 chosen warriors from Judah and Benjamin to fight Israel and get his kingdom back. That's not an army, friend. That's a whole stadium, and EVERY seat brought a sword.
But before anybody marches, the word of the LORD comes to Shemaiah, the man of God. It's a message for Rehoboam and all the Israelites in Judah and Benjamin.

cards.question: Rehoboam and his 180,000 warriors are ready to go. What does the LORD's message tell them?

answers.text: Wait for a sign then attack

cards.question: The LORD tells every man in Rehoboam's army to go home. What reason does He give?
Rehoboam's army was headed for Jeroboam son of Nebat, the man who came with all Israel to face Rehoboam (2 Chronicles 10:2-3). True or false: the army ignores the LORD's message and marches anyway.

cards.text: They listen to the words of the LORD and turn back. 180,000 warriors, all suited up, and everybody just goes HOME. Biggest "never mind" I ever heard, and I respect it.

cards.question: No war. So Rehoboam stays in Jerusalem and builds up cities in Judah for ___.

cards.text: The list runs from Bethlehem and Tekoa to Lachish and Hebron, fifteen fortified cities in Judah and Benjamin. He strengthens their fortifications and puts officers in every one, with supplies of food, oil and wine.

cards.question: Fifteen cities, each with officers and supplies. What else does Rehoboam put in all of them?

cards.text: He strengthens those cities greatly, and Judah and Benjamin belong to him. Walls up. Shields stacked. That's a man who learned to double-lock the door.
Rehoboam's cities are locked down tight. Then people start coming to him from all over Israel.

cards.question: From their districts all over Israel, a group comes to stand with Rehoboam. Who?
The Levites leave their pasturelands and possessions and go to Judah and Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons ___ them as priests of the LORD.

cards.text: Jeroboam appoints his own priests for the high places and for the goat demons and calf idols he had made. Goat DEMONS? I spent YEARS in a junk drawer, friend, and I never saw anything that bad.

cards.question: The Levites aren't the only ones heading to Jerusalem. Who follows them there?

answers.text: People from every tribe seeking the LORD
Soldiers from every tribe seeking pay
Merchants from every tribe seeking trade

cards.question: True or false: the people who follow the Levites come to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the LORD, the God of their fathers.

cards.text: All these newcomers strengthen the kingdom of Judah and support Rehoboam son of Solomon. Friend, most of us can't get ONE person to show up on moving day, and this man's got volunteers from EVERY tribe!

cards.question: They support Rehoboam for three years, because for three years they walk in the way of ___ and ___.

cards.text: Then comes Rehoboam's family. He loves Maacah daughter of Absalom more than all his wives and concubines, and in all he has eighteen wives, sixty concubines, twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters. EIGHTY-EIGHT children! I had six, and I never made it through one night without Chip asking for one more story.

cards.question: Out of twenty-eight sons, Rehoboam names one chief prince among his brothers. Who gets the job?
True or false: Rehoboam makes Abijah chief prince but plans to give the throne to another son.

cards.text: Then the text says it out loud: Rehoboam acted wisely. Write it down. Frame it. Hang it in the bakery.

cards.question: What wise move does Rehoboam make with some of his other sons?

answers.text: Spreads them through the fortified cities
Sends them off to serve Pharaoh

cards.text: He gives them abundant provisions and seeks many wives for them. Judah's strong and the family's set, but trust me, friend, this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: the 180,000 warriors line, 'That's not an army, friend.' and the stadium punchline. Non-opening story cards are limited to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question says 'The LORD tells every man in Rehoboam's army to go home.' The text addresses the message to 'Rehoboam son of Solomon king of Judah and all the Israelites in Judah and Benjamin' (11:3), not to the army specifically.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Card 7 has just established that the army does not march. This card adds no new part of the passage. It restates that they listened and turned back, then adds a joke, so it works as a recap of the answer instead of moving the passage forward.
This story card has 3 sentences. The limit is 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question begins 'No war. So Rehoboam stays in Jerusalem and builds up cities...' The word 'So' makes the cancelled war the reason for the building. 2 Chronicles 11:5 only says 'Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem, and he built up cities for defense in Judah' and gives no connection or reason.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'The list runs from Bethlehem and Tekoa to Lachish and Hebron' suggests the list ends with Lachish and Hebron. Lachish is 11th of the 15 cities, and Azekah, Zorah and Aijalon come after it (11:9-10).

rule.text: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: 'Write it down. Frame it. Hang it in the bakery.' treats Rehoboam acting wisely as a rare event worth framing. That laughs at Rehoboam instead of with his situation. The joke also depends on his earlier foolishness in 2 Chronicles 10, which this lesson never sets up.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: The joke works as a callback to Rehoboam's foolish choices in the previous passage. Nothing earlier in this lesson sets that up.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: The story-continues line 'trust me, friend, this story is NOT done' nearly copies the doc's example 'Trust me, friend, this story's not done.' instead of being an original line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: This summary card for the family stretch (11:18-21) has 4 sentences. The bite-sized rule limits non-opening story cards to 1 to 2 sentences. However, the doc's own good example of a long-stretch summary card (Genesis 5) has 4 sentences.
findings.question: Are long-stretch summary story cards held to the 1 to 2 sentence limit, or may they run longer, as the Genesis 5 example in prep-walkthrough.md does?
